svg.title: The Scramble for Africa & The Moroccan Crises (1884–1911)
svg.desc: KS3 historical GIS atlas map of Colonial Africa and South-West/Central Europe (1884–1914) paired with a zoomed 1:10m Morocco, Gibraltar, and Spain inset showing the 1884–85 Berlin Conference, the 1905 Tangier Crisis, the 1906 Algeciras Conference, the 1911 Agadir SMS Panther Crisis, British, French, German, and Belgian empires, and independent Abyssinia and Liberia.

5. German Colonies (“A Place in the Sun”)
Kamerun, E. & SW Africa fuel Weltpolitik & naval race

g.text: German Empire & Colonies (Kamerun, Togoland, E. & SW Africa)

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: CAUSES OF THE GREAT WAR
The Scramble for Africa & The Moroccan Crises (1884–1911)
After the 1884–85 Berlin Conference carved up 90% of Africa, Kaiser Wilhelm II’s Weltpolitik demanded "a place in the sun."
Instead of splitting the 1904 Entente, German brinkmanship at Tangier (1905), Algeciras (1906) & Agadir (1911) united Britain and France.
